parsed.rationale: All three initializers — `HSBColor.init(hue:saturation:brightness:)` in package `ColorPalette`, and `AccentColor.init(hue:saturation:brightness:)` plus `HSBOffset.init(hue:saturation:brightness:)` in package `Wallpaper` — share an identical signature. None of the participating records carry any restraint markers (is_test, is_mock, is_sample_app, is_codegen are all false). The duplication is structural and semantic: all three types represent HSB colour values and are initialised the same way. Introducing a protocol `HSBInitializable` with a required `init(hue:saturation:brightness:)` and a default implementation in a protocol extension would eliminate the repeated body and make the shared contract explicit. Because `ColorPalette` is already a dependency of `Wallpaper` (the `Wallpaper` package hosts types that consume colour abstractions), the protocol can live in `ColorPalette` and `Wallpaper`'s types can conform to it.
